comment.narrative: The distribution of the 29 women -led organisations is as follows; In Uganda the CSOs whose capacity were increased include POLLICY, Uganda Women Parliamentary Association , Democratic Governance Facility ,International of Women in Radio and Television-Uganda Chapter (IWART-U), Network for Women in Politics (NOWIP) Women's Pro Bono Initiative,Next Generation Women Initiative. Kenya the CSOs whose capacity was increased include Mzalendo Trust, Association of Media Women in Kenya (AMWIK), FEMNET, CRAWN Trust, the Communications and Strategy Lead - Office of the Vice President , the Young Women In Political Parties Leadership Kenya, Badili Africa. In Ethiopia the CSOs include Women from Standard for Integrated Development Ethiopia (SIDE), Ethiopia Insider,Ethiopian Women with Disability National Association, Ethiopian Citizens for Social Justice, Timran , Ethiopian women Rights Advocate; Ethiopian Civil Society Forum; Addis Powerhouse; Network of Ethiopian Women’s Associations (NEWA) and the Ethiopia Women Lawyers Asssociation. title.narrative: # of political/civic actors taken measures enhancing representation of women and youth

description.narrative: # of political/civic actors taken measures enhancing representation of women and youth

comment.narrative: A total of 29 civic and political actors in Uganda and Kenya took measures to enhance representation of women and youth. In Uganda the distribution of the 21 political and civic actors is follows 7 actors co-created measures they had taken in public media engagements (Interparty women’s platform, NOWIP, Women’s leagues, local Councilors, Media , Members of parliament, political parties); Increased funding for the International Women's Day(IWD) in the FDC political party-1; The Democratic Party Women's League facilitated the development of facilitated the development and adoption of the Gender Policy and Sexual Harassment Policy-1, AMwA facilitated the establishment of the Interparty Women's Platform that developed an MOU-1, 9 political and civic actors developed joint lobby and advocacy action-plans to advocate for inclusive political party systems and structures.( 6 political parties, NYC, Media, NIMD Ug), 1 political actor from National youth Council (NYC))moved the motion to pass the EAC SRHR Bill during the 5th East African Youth Parliament (EAYP), NYC developed a Communique-1. In Kenya, the distribution 8 actors political and civic actors is as follows Mzalendo Trust, FEMNET, CRAWN Trust, KEWOPA, Media, Badili Africa, UN women developed measures for increasing women and youth partcipation in political spaces There were no measures taken for enhancing representation of women and youth in Ethiopia and Sudan.
